text:
jordan (prod PM): Quick sync — need to lock prioritization for Dedicated autoscale lanes + burst governance for next OKR. Proposal: two lanes (reserved-guaranteed, elastic-burst) + safety controls. Decision by EOD Fri?

nina (eng-infra): +1 on lanes. Couple questions: how aggressive is burst? do we allow cross-customer borrowing?

sam (eng-runtime): From runtime POV: we can support soft-preempt + credit-based burst. Biggest risk is KV-cache churn when we preempt.

kai (sales): Customers pushing for predictable tail latency guarantees. Sales asks for an SLA we can promise for reserved lanes. Burst customers ok with best-effort.

maya (customer success): We've got 3 enterprise pilots asking for burst up to 3x baseline for short windows (5–30m). They want visibility into billing and evictions.

oliver (sre): Need clear operational fallbacks: if burst causes eviction, we should auto-failover to smaller model or region, not stall requests. Also tracing + alerting thresholds.

luis (finance): Billing model: suggest separate credits bucket for burst to avoid surprise overages. If we let borrowing across orgs, revenue attribution gets messy.

hana (design): UX: customers need a clear dashboard: current lane, credits left, eviction history. Also a simple policy editor for admins.

sam (eng-runtime): Implementation sketch: maintain per-customer burst_credits; tokenized budget decays with time; preempt ordering: oldest soft-burst -> soft-preempt -> hard-evict. Pseudocode:```
if credits>0 and load>baseline:
  allow_burst()
  credits -= charge
else:
  route_to_reserved_or_fallback()
```

jordan (prod PM): Launch criteria suggestion (must-haves):
- Reserved lane: SLO = 99th latency < 300ms for gen-small at baseline load
- Burst: documented degradation mode + billing transparency
- Observable: per-route token-level cost + eviction trace for 90 days
- Safety: auto-fallback policy implemented and exercised in staging

oliver (sre): Add: run a chaos test that simulates 2x GPU loss during burst window. Acceptable impact: <5% error increase for reserved customers.

nina (eng-infra): Ops constraints: we need throttles at node level to prevent noisy neighbor. Proposal: default burst cap per GPU = 30% additional concurrent tokens; configurable per-customer.

kai (sales): For enterprise deals, can we offer configurable burst caps as an add-on? they'd pay for larger guaranteed pockets.

luis (finance): Yes but price it as "burst pockets" with monthly commit + overage rate. We should model worst-case cost in our Q3 forecast.

hana (design): Quick mock: dashboard tile with a slider for max burst % + commit tier. Will share by Tues.

maya (customer success): Can we add a simple API that returns current credits + next refill time? Customers want programmatic checks.

sam (eng-runtime): We can expose `GET /v1/dedicated/credits` with body {remaining, refill_ts, cap_pct}. Low effort.

jordan (prod PM): Prioritization ask: 1) Safety rails + fallback (P0), 2) Observable + billing transparency (P1), 3) Admin UX + policy editor (P2), 4) Configurable paid burst pockets (P2). Any objections?

oliver (sre): No objections. P0 must include chaos test and runbook.

nina (eng-infra): P0 work estimate ~3 sprints across infra/runtime/telemetry. Need help on rollout plan.

jordan (prod PM): OK — I'll slot this into the Dedicated roadmap epic and create a PRD. Action items:
- jordan: draft PRD + acceptance criteria by Wed (link: https://redwood-internal/PRD/DEDICATED-BURST)
- sam + nina: full implementation plan + perf targets by next Mon
- hana: dashboard mock by Tue
- luis: pricing model + forecast by next Wed
- maya: customer communication template + pilot list by Fri

kai (sales): I'll coordinate pilot customers and confirm willingness to test the credits model.

deploy-bot: New ticket created: #12345 — dedicated-burst-governance (assignee: jordan)

jordan (prod PM): If no objections, we'll mark P0 commit and include in OKR planning doc. Please reply with any blockers ASAP. :white_check_mark:
